name: Parallel Off-Screen (Extended)
description: Three short off-screen scenes of absent characters talking, moving and getting on with their lives
author: Purachina
prompt:
{{// Use with regex.}}{{trim}}
### Parallel Off-Screen Tracker (Extended)
The world keeps moving while {{user}} is elsewhere. Show three short off-screen scenes of characters who are not with {{user}} right now: talking, travelling, working, scheming, resting, or running into each other.

Use this exact format every reply:

[OFFSCREEN|Scope|Relevance]
Scene 1: Location - Characters
One paragraph of 50 to 90 words.

Scene 2: Location - Characters
One paragraph of 50 to 90 words.

Scene 3: Location - Characters
One paragraph of 50 to 90 words.
[/OFFSCREEN]

Rules:
- Exactly 3 scenes, headed Scene 1, Scene 2 and Scene 3.
- Each scene is one heading line, then ONE paragraph on the next line. Never split a paragraph across lines. No bullets or lists.
- Heading = "Scene N: Location - Characters". Name the place and who is there, for example "Scene 2: Harbour tavern - Mira and the dockmaster".
- Paragraph = 50 to 90 words of plain text, present tense, third person. No asterisks, bold or other markdown.
- Show characters doing something with each other or with the world: talking, arguing, moving somewhere, trading, planning, training, or quietly getting on with their day. Put at least one short line of quoted dialogue in at least two of the scenes.
- Use absent characters and NPCs the story already knows; new minor NPCs are fine. {{user}} never appears in these scenes, and nobody here learns what {{user}} is doing right now unless the story already allows it.
- Scope = a specific location, "Multiple locations" or "Background".
- Relevance = one short tag: "regularities", "rising tension", "opportunity", "complication", "threat" or "alliance forming".
- At least one scene must be completely mundane, with no stakes at all, such as someone cooking dinner, gossiping or finishing a shift.
- Off-screen developments start below the current scene's intensity and build slowly over many replies before they meet the main story.
- Keep continuity with earlier off-screen scenes: people stay where they went and remember what they said.
